output.summary: Submerged marine flowering plant native to northern-latitude coastlines of North America and Eurasia. Its hairlike leaves grow from rhizomes that can spread into seabed meadows; one cloned meadow was genetically estimated at 3,000 years old. The Seri people of Mexico eat the grains toasted and ground into paste, while a Spanish chef has cultivated them in Cádiz as “sea rice.”
output.edibilityNote: The Seri toast and grind the grains into paste; a Spanish chef has cultivated and harvested them as “sea rice” in Cádiz.
